discussion_comments.comment_body: Done in 03771416 — collapsed the includes("/") + indexOf("/") pair into a single indexOf with a -1 check, and dropped the redundant `as string` cast (typeof guard already narrows the type). Tests still pass. Thanks for the suggestion.

Thanks for the suggestion. The executor module legitimately uses these constants because it has many call sites. The validator function uses the URL once and the User-Agent once, so introducing module-scope constants for a single call site adds indirection without a real DRY benefit. If chatgpt.com changes its UA expectations, the executor's UA constant is the load-bearing one — the validator's UA only matters during account validation. Leaving as-is intentionally.

Fixed — removed `MULTI_SPACE` and `MULTI_NL` replacements from `cleanResponse()`. Now only trims leading/trailing whitespace, preserving all markdown formatting (code blocks, tables, indentation). Good catch, this would have mangled code-heavy responses.

The explicit assignment is intentional for readability — it makes the passthrough path symmetric with the other branches (`nativeCodexPassthrough` and the else branch). Now updated to `{ ...body }` to avoid mutation, which also makes the value differ from the initial `let translatedBody = body`.

While a shared base config could reduce lines, it would create implicit coupling between providers that may evolve independently (different auth schemes, custom headers, unique parseResponse logic).
